title: InterpreSure Suggestions
description: Pragmatic analysis of a Bible translation passage. Evaluates how well the translation preserves the pragmatic meaning of the original — implicatures, presuppositions, information structure, social dynamics, and scalar nuances. Can be anchored at verse or chapter level. Chapter-level items summarize the full chapter.

strengths.description: What the translation does well pragmatically. Each item is a single concrete observation. May be empty.

weaknesses.description: Areas where pragmatic meaning is lost, distorted, or over-explicated. Each item is a single concrete observation. May be empty.

suggestions.description: Concrete actionable improvements in plain language. Each item is a single suggestion. May be empty.

score.description: Overall pragmatic fidelity score. 1 = substantial meaning loss, 10 = all in-line and between-the-lines meaning preserved.

reasoning.description: Markdown-formatted technical reasoning. Explains the pragmatic analysis of the original and how the translation handles those dynamics. May cite Greek/Hebrew from the source text and words/phrases from the translation. Should note how expert annotations, BART, and MACULA data (if available) influenced the assessment.

cross_references.description: U23003 scripture references the model consulted during analysis (e.g. cross-chapter or cross-book references). Empty if none were used.

verses_to_review.description: For chapter-level items only: verse numbers within the chapter that need the most translator attention. Empty for verse-level items.
